newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mystery fumes at Japan school, 79 taken to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Mystery fumes at Japan school, 79 taken to hospital.

text.p: Dozens of children were taken to hospital complaining of sore throats and streaming eyes on Thursday after mysterious pungent fumes caused panic at a Tokyo junior high school, emergency services said.
Fire Department officials said 79 students were taken to hospital after breathing in fumes that spread through the school building. The nature and source of the fumes was not immediately clear.
But the officials said the students only suffered sore throats and watery eyes and none of them were seriously harmed.

In addition to the children taken to hospital, another 50 students were examined by paramedics at the campus of the junior high school in Fukagawa, eastern Tokyo, whose students range in age from 13 to 15.
Fire Department officials said staff and children at the school, which has 635 students, were thrown into a state of panic by the fumes, with children pouring out of classes.
The officials said there were no chemical experiments being conducted in the school laboratory and no chemical factories nearby which could have been the source of the fumes.

Last year, there were several cases of mysterious fumes in public places, which police said were the work of pranksters using cans of spray mace, a substance commonly used in self-defence to temporarily debilitate an attacker.
Those incidents followed a nerve gas attack on the Tokyo subway in March that year which killed 12 people and made another 6,000 ill.
The leader and followers of the doomsday cult Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) are on trial for the subway attack.
